intro:
VORONEZH (22 OCTOBER 1919)

Comrade Commander, Denikin's advance has brought the White armies towards Moscow, but their widening front has left a flank exposed at Voronezh. Our Eighth Army is still fighting on the Don, and reinforcements are coming from the north.

Bring your cavalry corps against Voronezh from the west. Take the crossings and junctions before the White command can reinforce them. A breakthrough here will threaten the side of the army advancing on the capital.

briliant.text: What a beautiful day, comrade!  The smell of capitalists fleeing from the people's army is in the air.  Voronezh is liberated but the enemy is not yet fully defeated.  Start the pursuit immediately!

intro:
ROSTOV (6 January 1920)

The White armies are falling back towards the Don. Rostov controls the roads into the Caucasus, and their retreating formations need its crossings to stay connected.

Take Rostov before they can organise a defence around the city. Use the cavalry to reach the junctions ahead of the retreat. The following formations need those roads open if the offensive is to continue south.

briliant.text:
Yes, comrade. This is an impressive piece of mobile warfare! You were even faster in Rostov than some of the capitalist's troops! Roam the countryside and liberate the towns and villages of the provinces from the capitalists and monarchists. They deserve to be free! Hunt down every last traitor of the people!

AFTERMATH:
By the end of 1919 the White armies in Siberia, western Russia and the Ukraine had been contained and defeated by the victorious Red Army. Although isolated troops and bands continued to roam around, the only organized resistance was put up by General Wrangel on the Crimea. However, with peace so close by for the Bolshevik government, the tide seemed to turn again and not for the better...

intro:
BATTLE OF VOLODARKA (29 May 1920)

Your divisions have reached the Polish front south of Kiev. The enemy's advance has taken the city, but its line through the countryside is stretched between widely separated positions.

Force a passage near Volodarka and open it for the infantry following your cavalry. The Third Don Cossack Brigade is coming to support the attack. A breach here would threaten the roads behind the Polish troops at Kiev.

briliant.text:
Comrade, the operation near Volodarka has not been a success. The Polish troops had cowardly tactics and hid themselves in the villages where our horses have little effect! However the fighting with the Polish cavalry showed that the people's Cavalry Army is a superior army!

There is more bad news. The reason why you lost contact with the Don Cossacks Brigade was not your fault, comrade. It seems that they have switched sides and have joined the capitalist criminals that we are fighting! I urge you to make clear to your men the fate of such traitors!

intro:
KIEV COUNTEROFFENSIVE (9 June 1920)

Our offensive north and south of Kiev has forced the Polish armies back. The Twelfth Army is approaching from the east; your cavalry is in position to threaten the roads out of the city from the south.

Take Kiev, establish contact with the Twelfth Army and carry the advance west. Reach the crossings before the retreating troops can destroy them. Without those bridges, the infantry and guns will struggle to follow the cavalry.

briliant.text:
Comrade! Kiev is liberated! Imagine the headline of tomorrow's newspaper! "The Ukrainian capital has been liberated!" The people of the Ukraine are now free from the capitalists who have ruled them for the past few weeks.

Also, I assume you know what to do with the Ukrainian prisoners of war? They are traitors of their own people. They allied themselves with the very power that invaded their country and they deserve nothing but the final penalty.

intro:
DELAY AT ROVNO (1 July 1920)

The advance from Kiev has brought us to Rovno. Lwow remains the army's direction, but Polish troops are holding the junctions along the route and fighting to gain time for another line farther west.

Take Rovno and the communications centres around it. Keep the roads between the divisions open as the advance continues. The horses need food as urgently as the guns need ammunition; a column cut off from its supplies will soon lose its speed.

briliant.text:
Do not apologize, comrade. Although you were held up near Rovno, the advance is still under way. Not even the people's army can win every skirmish. But the war, comrade, the war is still going on, and it is going in our favor!

I have received more good news. Comrade Tukhachevsky has started a grand offensive in Belarus and is also moving west! Capitalist Poland will suffer dearly for their attack on the people of Russia!

intro:
Brody — 29 July 1920

The First Cavalry Army has reached Brody on the road towards Lwow. Polish formations have fallen back, but they can still gather against the gaps between our extended divisions.

Secure Brody and the surrounding junctions. Bring the horse artillery forward as the cavalry clears the approaches. The next advance depends on keeping the divisions connected through this road network.

briliant.text:
You have fended off disaster, comrade. The Poles conducted a flanking attack on Brody while our eyes were pointed only on getting to Lwow. You stabilized the situation!

On the other side, it was sarcastic that you had to encounter the treacherous Don Cossacks again that left our side at Volodarka. If they had only known that the Revolution cannot be turned around. We will make sure they know now.

Keep advancing towards Lwow. It is not far now!

intro:
BATTLE OF ZADWORZE (17 August 1920)

Lwow is close, but cavalry cannot take a defended city without infantry and a reliable supply route. Zadworze's railway junction stands between our leading regiments and the support following them.

Take the junction and open the line. We do not yet know the strength of the force holding it. Clear the approaches quickly enough for the infantry and guns to come forward before Lwow's defenders can complete their preparations.

briliant.text: Well, if you like to see it that way.  The Poles were brave for defending that village to the bitter end but it turned into a Polish Thermopylae.  It only shows the superiority of the people's army!  The capitalists from London, Paris and Warsaw are sending their slaves to a certain death in order to stop us.  Yet they fail in stopping us!  They only slowed us down for a single day.  What is a single day in a war?  Go comrade, Lwow is ours!

intro:
LWOW (20 August 1920)

The city is ahead of us, Comrade. Our formations are closing on Lwow from the north and east, with the Fourteenth Army's infantry following the cavalry.

Enter the city and take the positions controlling its approaches. Prisoners report that the delay at Zadworze has given the defenders time to prepare. Keep contact with the infantry; the streets will give the enemy chances that the open country did not.

briliant.text: For three days blood was shed and both sides have suffered massive casualties.  Lwow is still in reactionary hands.  You have done well despite the results, comrade.  But reports I am getting show a very, very grave situation is on our hands...

intro:
BATTLE OF KOMAROW (29 August 1920)

The Polish counteroffensive has broken through between Lwow and Warsaw. Our northern armies are retreating to avoid encirclement, and the cavalry has been ordered away from Lwow to help restore the front.

Break the line at Komarow and push north towards our retreating armies. The Polish forces have used our change of direction to place troops across the route. Open it before their pressure separates the two halves of the front completely.

briliant.text:
Here, quickly, comrade! A squadron of our loyal Cossacks have made a corridor through which we can escape! Though not mauled, we have suffered a moral defeat from the Polish cavalry. Worst of all, we have been denied access to the north and our entire front in Poland is rapidly collapsing...

NOTEWORTHY: Because of the numbers of forces involved, the Battle of Komarow is considered the greatest cavalry battle of the 20th century. Also it was the last battle fought mostly by cavalry units, in which traditional cavalry tactics were used and sabers and lances played a vital role.

intro:
RETREAT FROM ROVNO (18 September 1920)

The campaign has turned against us. Polish troops hold Rovno and are extending their counteroffensive into the south. Our divisions need time to recover, but they will not get it while the enemy closes around them here.

Bring the army east through the withdrawal routes. Keep the scattered regiments together and cover the crossings until the guns and supply columns are clear. We can reorganise an army that gets away; we cannot replace one left in a pocket.

briliant.text:
Our armies are safe, comrade. Thanks to your excellent rearguard duty slowing down the Polish army in the south long enough for us to retreat to better positions. The front is stabilizing again locally. Plus I have orders for our command to be pulled out of the frontline. That means rest and refitting for the first time in months!

---Some weeks later at the local HQ---

Good news, comrade! The capitalists in Warsaw realize that further struggles with the People's Republic will inevitably will lead their defeat! Though not all of our claims have been recognized in the cease fire, we now have peace at our western borders! That means we finally have a border instead of a front!

Sadly that is not true for the southern border...

intro:
KAKHOVKA (20 October 1920)

Wrangel has pushed out of the Crimea while our attention was on Poland. His troops are spread across the country north of Perekop, with the narrow isthmus behind them as their route back to the peninsula.

Cross the Dnieper near Kakhovka and break into their rear. The cavalry must reach the routes towards Perekop before the White columns do. Cut them off from the fortified entrance to the Crimea.

briliant.text: Comrade, what can I say!  Moscow expected a long campaign against Wrangel. However your horses have proven them wrong!  The enemy is shattered.  Our people's armies are closing in on them.  Now quickly!  To the Perekop isthmus!!!

intro:
PEREKOP (28 October 1920)

Our advance is nearing Perekop. White formations are falling back towards the isthmus, where a narrow front would allow them to hold with far fewer men.

Press on and force a passage into the Crimea before the retreating troops can settle behind those defences. Other armies are clearing the pockets farther north; their troops will join you as they become available. Until then, the speed of your cavalry is our best chance.

briliant.text: We must not stop now!  We have forced our way over the Perekop isthmus.  Not only is Moscow happy with your results but also the glorious people's army.  Now Wrangel is not in the position to cause more bloodshed.  Blood of the Russian proletariat!  Go forward and hunt down the enemy criminals!

intro:
Sevastopol — 11 November 1920

The northern approaches to the Crimea are open, and Wrangel's troops are withdrawing towards the ports. Ships off Sevastopol offer them a way to carry an army away even after the peninsula is lost.

Advance on the port and clear the positions along the roads into it. The cavalry can reach the approaches quickly, but the rearguards still have guns and machine guns. Take the last base before they can turn the streets into another defensive line.

briliant.text: Comrade, this is one of the finest bottles of vodka!  Something that Wrangel wanted to take with him in his escape.  Though Wrangel has escaped, something historical has happened, comrade.  The Revolution of the proletariat in Russia has succeeded!  For the first time in history, the socialists of the people will rule themselves!  No more tyranny, no more social classes!  We will all be equal!  A dream has come alive, comrade!
